statement: Find the coefficient of $x^{n}$ in the expansion of $(1+x)^{2n}$, and show that this coefficient is even for every integer $n\ge1$.
solution: The coefficient of $x^{n}$ in $(1+x)^{2n}$ is $\binom{2n}{n}$. Using $\binom{2n}{n}=\dfrac{2n}{n}\binom{2n-1}{n-1}=2\binom{2n-1}{n-1}$, it is exactly twice an integer, hence even for all $n\ge1$.
